messages:
mike: Posting perfetto + nsys traces from the 20ms continuous-batch experiment — tail latency spikes around 1.2-1.8s into the run. Link: https://perfetto/reports/abcd (redacted)

mike: High-level: median is fine, p99 jumps ~4x after a brief steady state. I suspect kernel switchover + scheduler preemption causing queue time to balloon.

anna: can you attach the nsys timeline screenshot? also which model / quant profile?

mike: Model: llama-13b-quant (int8-qi). Config: batch_window_ms=20, batch_max_tokens=2048, kv_cache_enabled=true

mike: here's the nsys command I used:
```bash
nsys profile --output=run1 --trace=nvtx,cuda --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi ./run_infer_runner.sh
```

raj: quick glance at the nvtx regions shows a long host-queue idle while CUDA kernels are short — suspicious dispatcher preemption. Grepping the runtime logs shows a coincident kernel_choice switch:
```
$ grep kernel_choice runtime.log | tail -n 6
[12:34:01] kernel_choice: matmul_fp16_opt selected
[12:34:01] kernel_choice: matmul_fp16_opt selected
[12:34:02] kernel_choice: matmul_fallback selected  <-- switch
[12:34:02] kv_cache: miss for key 0x7fabc
[12:34:02] batch_window: flushed early
```

lisa: kv cache miss + fallback kernel at the same timestamp. Could be eviction / sweep running during heavy coalescing. Are sweeps happening on the scheduler thread?

mike: perfetto slice shows host thread blocked ~3ms waiting on allocator lock, then multiple small kernels scheduled across streams, then the fallback matmul runs and dominates tail latency. (attached view link)

anna: hypothesis: the 20ms continuous batching window allows large coalesced batches to overlap with background work (kv-sweep), leading to fragmented workspace and kernel selection falling back. Try batch_window_ms=8 and pin kernel_affinity to prefer stream 0.

raj: also try disabling background kv sweep for the test: export REDWOOD_KV_SWEEP=0 and re-run.

mike: ran quick experiments: batch_window_ms=8 -> p99 drops ~42%; REDWOOD_KV_SWEEP=0 -> p99 drops further ~18%. Forcing kernel_affinity=preferred -> no fallback observed in logs.

lisa: good data. Can we capture exact condition that triggers fallback? maybe kernel selection queries workspace and sees insufficient contiguous memory due to transient allocations.

mike: found lines in allocator debug showing workspace checks: "workspace_needed=98MB, free_contiguous=70MB -> fallback". So fragmentation + preempted allocations causing workspace shortfall.

anna: plan: (1) add NVTX markers around kv-sweep and allocator ops, (2) reserve a small contiguous slab for matmul kernels in allocator, (3) reduce max batch coalescing when kv sweep active.

mike: I'll schedule a full perf run (perfetto + nsys + allocator debug) in staging for 30m and tag infra. @julia can you reserve a node with same hw profile?

deploy-bot: deploy logged: perf/allocator-debug -> staging at 12:50 UTC :white_check_mark:

julia: happy to help, reserving a 8xA100 node now and enabling nvlink counters. Will attach access details when ready.

mike: thanks — will post the trace + short summary after the run. :thumbsup:
